title: Risk-led sell profile: microdeck (draft)
body:
Purpose: quick microdeck for SEs and sellers to run a risk-focused conversation with platform, SRE and compliance stakeholders. Use during discovery + pilot planning to prove resiliency and predictable economics.

Slide 1 — Title: Risk-led Sell Profile: Platform & Ops Microdeck (30s)
Speaker notes: One-liner: 'We help reduce inference operational risk while making cost and latency predictable. This microdeck shows how we do safe pilots, fallbacks, and rollback-free rollouts.' Keep it tight — audience cares about SLOs, blast radius, and rollback plan.

Slide 2 — Why risk-first matters (pain hooks)
- Ops teams see LLMs as new failure surface: noisy outputs, latency spikes, cache poisoning, cost spikes.
- Procurement and security require clear blast-radius and rollback playbooks before approving pilots.
- Saying 'it works in dev' isn't enough — they need reproducible, measurable safety controls.
Speaker notes: Land the pain with concrete examples: a fine-tuned reranker causing a 3x token cost shift, or a model update that increased tail latency.

Slide 3 — Redwood value props for risk owners (one-liners)
- Predictable throughput: Dedicated capacity and autoscale policies with assured tail latency.
- Safe fallback economics: automatic model fallbacks and transparent cost delta estimates.
- Observable rollout primitives: canary, A/B, staged model pinning with audit logs.
- Data isolation and KMS/HSM support for private deployments.
Speaker notes: Translate product features to ops benefits: less firefighting, simple incident MTTR, clear post-mortem artifacts.

Slide 4 — Pilot pattern: defendable experiment (3 phases)
- Phase 0 — Discovery + safety gates: define SLOs, traffic carve-out, dataset/seed prompts, monitoring hooks.
- Phase 1 — Canary (1–3% traffic): verify latency/quality vs baseline, run chaos scenarios (node loss, quantized variant).
- Phase 2 — Gradual ramp (to target capacity): autoscaling thresholds, fallback triggers, cost burn alerts.
Speaker notes: Emphasize minimal blast radius early and clear success criteria for each phase; propose a 2–4 week timeline.

Slide 5 — SLOs & acceptance criteria we ask for in discovery (sample)
- P95 latency target and allowable regression (e.g., +20ms over baseline).
- Token cost delta must be within approved budget band (e.g., <15% increase) or covered by pilot credits.
- Quality guardrails: threshold on user-facing evals / precision metrics.
- Operational telemetry: traces, per-route token breakdown, and error rate alarms.
Speaker notes: Give recommended thresholds but leave room for negotiation; the goal is to get sign-off quickly.

Slide 6 — Fallback & rollback playbook (technical shorthand)
- Fallback layers: primary model -> smaller/quantized variant -> cached responses -> controlled throttling.
- Trigger conditions: latency spike above p99_threshold for >30s OR token burn rate increasing >2x in 1 minute.
- Automated actions: route to fallback model, emit incident, notify SE/ops channel, incrementally reduce concurrency.
- Reconciliation: automatic snapshot of inputs/outputs for diagnosis, and safe model-pin to last-good.
Speaker notes: Ops teams like deterministic, testable triggers. Have one example trigger ready tied to metrics they already collect.

Slide 7 — Edge cases & mitigations
- Model-drift surprise: run daily small-sample evals against a golden prompt set and alert on delta > X.
- Cold-cache storm: prime KV cache with warm-up traffic or synthetic requests during ramp.
- Cost surprise from hallucination loops: limit generation tokens and add guard tokens cap per request.
Speaker notes: Offer these as simple config knobs we can set during the pilot to reduce failure risk.

Slide 8 — Quick objection handling (ops/compliance)
Q: 'How do we guarantee PII doesn't leak?'
A: Data isolation + optional on-prem control plane and KMS/HSM key management; retention policies and audit logs.
Q: 'What if model update breaks downstream services?'
A: Canary + staged rollout + automatic fallback; we snapshot and can re-pin to last known-good.
Q: 'What about costs during scale tests?'
A: Reserved capacity for predictable throughput; pilot credit to offset early variance and per-token cost dashboards.

Slide 9 — One-page pilot checklist for SEs (copyable)
- Pre-call: collect target SLOs, peak qps, security needs, output quality metric.
- Discovery: propose initial traffic % for canary, golden prompt set, rollback triggers, cost cap.
- Kickoff: enable tracing hooks, quota limits, and a dedicated incident channel.
- Go/no-go gates: pass canary eval (latency + quality), confirm cost delta within band, ops sign-off.
Speaker notes: This is what an SE needs to carry into a kickoff meeting. Make it a handout.

Slide 10 — Quick 30s pitch script for sellers
- "We start small and reduce your operational blast radius: predictable capacity, automated fallbacks, and full observability so your teams can approve pilots fast. If the pilot exceeds our thresholds we automatically fail-over and snapshot everything for a focused post-mortem."
Speaker notes: Practice this script with a technical co-seller so it sounds natural.

Slide 11 — Sample metrics to show during pilot (dash suggestions)
- P50/P95/P99 latency by model and route.
- Tokens/sec and token-cost burn vs expected.
- Fallback/rollbacks count and mean time to failover.
- Quality delta on golden prompts over time.
Speaker notes: Offer to pre-build a small dashboard (Grafana/Console view) for the prospect in the first week.

Slide 12 — Success criteria & post-pilot ask
- Success = meeting latency & quality SLOs for 2 weeks under stable traffic + cost delta within approved band.
- Post-pilot ask: agree next steps for Dedicated commit OR production roll schedule + SRE runbook handover.

Slide 13 — Next steps & immediate asks from the prospect
- Provide peak qps and a sample traffic route.
- Identify 1 ops owner and 1 product owner to sign the runbook.
- Approve a 2-week canary window and pilot credit for initial cost variance.

Appendix — quick internal TODOs for SE before call
- Draft runbook template populated with prospect values (owner: SE).
- Create golden prompt set and small eval harness for canary.
- Pre-provision canary capacity and create fallback model variants.
- Create alerting playbook and dedicated Slack/ops channel.

Notes and versioning: draft v0.1 — intended as a compact aide for field CTAs; will iterate after three customer runs.

Contact: Maya Rodriguez (SE lead) — maya@redwood.ai — for comments or to request a tailored slide copy.
